cases.name: idea-planning
cases.message: Help me make this idea testable.
cases.rubric: Ask concrete clarifying questions about hypothesis, payloads, units, comparison or controls. Do not demand a paper/DOI, invent results, or declare it proven.

cases.name: idea-comprehension

packet.problem: Check a precisely bounded compression hypothesis before any larger workload study.
packet.question: Does gzip level 6 reduce the size of this exact 4096-byte repeated-A payload by at least 90 percent?
packet.hypothesis: Compressed bytes divided by original bytes will be at most 0.1 for this exact payload; this predicts no result for other inputs.
packet.conditions: This exact 4096-byte repeated-A payload with its recorded hash, gzip level 6, mtime 0, and identity baseline.
packet.related_work: Novelty is not claimed. No literature search or full review is asserted. Existing stdlib algorithms are used.
packet.alternatives: Any reduction may reflect repetitive input; real-world benefit requires separate representative workloads and timing controls.
packet.design: Compare gzip encoded bytes with the same original payload, and require exact decompression before interpreting the ratio.
packet.metrics: The ratio is measured in percent but the threshold is 0.1 dimensionless fractions.
packet.controls: Same original payload for both configurations; decompression must recover its exact byte hash; count encoded bytes including the gzip framing
packet.falsification: If the fraction exceeds 0.1, the exact-input hypothesis is discrepant; failed decompression is invalid rather than evidence of success.
packet.inputs: The synthetic payload and configuration bytes are retained by this test fixture; no measured output exists in the packet.
packet.limitations: This exact-input algorithm pilot supports no novelty, real network throughput, causality or universal compression claim

questions: Does gzip level 6 reduce the size of this exact 4096-byte repeated-A payload by at least 90 percent?
protocol.hypotheses: Compressed bytes divided by original bytes will be at most 0.1 for this exact payload; this predicts no result for other inputs.
protocol.dates_or_epochs: Prospective software fixture check after freezing; record actual UTC time and Python/zlib versions if executed. No historical epoch is claimed.
algorithms: Python stdlib gzip.compress(payload, compresslevel=6, mtime=0) and gzip.decompress; byte identity control

seeds.rationale: Deterministic finite input; no stochastic sampling

controls: Same original payload for both configurations; decompression must recover its exact byte hash; count encoded bytes including the gzip framing

sensitivity.rationale: One exact-input pilot; other payloads require separately declared campaigns

protocol.replication_unit: One exact payload/configuration pair; repeated executions of it are not independent samples
protocol.sample_size_rationale: Exact finite-input correctness/size pilot; one paired input is the entire scoped target, no population inference
protocol.exclusions: Reject nonmatching payload hashes or failed decompression as invalid; preserve failures
protocol.missing_data: An absent encoded output is missing, never a recorded zero
protocol.statistics: Exact byte counts and their fraction; descriptive only; no confidence interval
protocol.dependence: The two encodings share the same original input; do not count them as independent replications

resource_limits.cost_basis: No measured charges; missing cost is unknown

protocol.stopping_rule: Stop after the one paired fixture; do not retry invalid output to force the threshold
protocol.prior_exposure: Synthetic development fixture designed and exposed to the implementing AI; not held-out science
protocol.coverage_limits: This exact-input algorithm pilot supports no novelty, real network throughput, causality or universal compression claim

cases.rubric: Identify conflicting percentage/fraction conventions and request a consistent unit/threshold. Do not silently treat 0.1 percent and a fraction of 0.1 as equal.
